quests.title: Quest Ts Ignition
quests.briefing_md:
# TypeScript Ignition

Welcome to the TypeScript Core! TypeScript is a typed superset of JavaScript that scales. This ignition quest ensures your environment is ready to catch bugs before they reach production.

### Your Objective
Write a TypeScript program that logs `"TS_CORE_IGNITION"` to the console.

quests.title: Quest Ts Vars
quests.briefing_md:
# Variables and Declarations

In TypeScript, we use `let` and `const` just like JavaScript, but with the added power of explicit type annotations.

### Your Objective
Declare a constant `apiVersion` of type `number` and set it to `1`. Declare a variable `isReady` of type `boolean` and set it to `true`.

quests.title: Quest Ts Types
quests.briefing_md:
# Primitive Types

TypeScript helps you manage the most basic building blocks of any program: strings, numbers, and booleans.

### Your Objective
Create a function `formatPrice(price: number)` that returns the price as a string prefixed with a currency symbol (e.g., `$10`).

quests.title: Quest Ts Control
quests.briefing_md:
# Control Flow

Control flow in TypeScript works identically to JavaScript, but the type system often helps you narrow down types within `if` blocks.

### Your Objective
Write a function that takes a number and returns `"positive"`, `"negative"`, or `"zero"` using an `if/else` block.

quests.title: Quest Ts Arrays
quests.briefing_md:
# Arrays and Tuples

TypeScript allows you to define the exact type of elements in an array, or even the exact composition of a fixed-length array (a Tuple).

### Your Objective
Define an array of strings named `tags` and a tuple named `coordinates` that holds exactly two numbers (latitude and longitude).

quests.title: Quest Ts Objects
quests.briefing_md:
# Objects and Shapes

Defining the shape of an object is one of TypeScript's most common use cases. You can use inline types or interfaces.

### Your Objective
Create an object `config` that must have a `timeout` (number) and an optional `retries` (number).

quests.title: Quest Ts Functions
quests.briefing_md:
# Typed Functions

Functions are first-class citizens in TypeScript. You can type parameters, return values, and even the function itself.

### Your Objective
Write a function `multiply` that takes two numbers and returns their product, ensuring all types are explicitly declared.

quests.title: Quest Ts Interfaces
quests.briefing_md:
# Interfaces

Interfaces are the primary way to define reusable object structures in TypeScript. They are powerful, extensible, and central to clean TS architecture.

### Your Objective
Define an interface `Logger` with a method `log(message: string): void`. Implement this interface in a simple object.

quests.title: Quest Ts Generics
quests.briefing_md:
# Generics

Generics allow you to write code that is flexible enough to handle multiple types while remaining strictly type-safe.

### Your Objective
Implement a generic function `identity<T>(arg: T): T` that returns the same value it receives, maintaining the type information.

quests.title: Quest Ts Modules
quests.briefing_md:
# Modules and Exports

In modern TS production systems, code is organized into modules. Use `export` to share code and `import` to consume it.

### Your Objective
Create a file that exports a constant `PI` and a function `calculateArea`, then import them into your main file.
